questions.question: Which command displays the commit history of a Git repository?
questions.explanation: `git log` lists all commits in reverse chronological order with author, date, and commit message.

questions.question: Which flag condenses each commit into a single line showing its short hash and message?
questions.explanation: `git log --oneline` provides a clean, single-line overview of commits ideal for quickly scanning project history.

questions.question: How do you exit when `git log` opens a scrollable pager in your terminal?
questions.explanation: Git uses the `less` terminal pager for long outputs. Pressing `q` immediately quits the pager.

questions.question: What does the command `git diff` (without extra flags) display?

options.A: Differences between your working directory and the staging area (unstaged changes)
options.B: Differences between staged changes and the last commit
options.C: Differences between your local branch and GitHub

questions.explanation: By default, `git diff` shows unstaged changes in your working tree compared to what is currently in the staging area.

questions.question: Which command shows differences that have been staged for the next commit?
questions.explanation: `git diff --staged` (or `git diff --cached`) compares changes currently in the staging area against the latest commit.

questions.question: In `git diff` output, what do lines starting with a `+` symbol indicate?
questions.explanation: Lines prefixed with `+` (typically highlighted green) represent added or replaced content, while `-` represents removed lines.

questions.question: What is a Git commit hash (SHA-1 checksum)?

options.A: A random password generated by GitHub
options.B: A unique 40-character cryptographic identifier representing the commit snapshot and metadata
options.C: The user ID of the person committing
options.D: The number of lines in the commit

questions.explanation: Git hashes are 40-character hexadecimal strings generated from commit content and metadata, guaranteeing integrity.

questions.question: What special pointer in Git represents your current location / latest commit on the active branch?
questions.explanation: `HEAD` is a symbolic reference pointer to the current commit/branch you are currently working on.

questions.question: Which command displays the full metadata and diff of the most recent commit?
questions.explanation: `git show <commit>` (or `git show HEAD`) displays the author, date, commit message, and full patch diff of that commit.

questions.question: Which commit message follows professional best practices?

options.B: fix: resolve navigation bar alignment on mobile screens

questions.explanation: Good commit messages are descriptive, use an imperative tone, and clearly summarize what changed and why.
